study: Lightweight detection of visible instruction injections in synthetic resume text
gap: The anchor's small synthetic evaluation does not establish whether a trained text detector generalizes to held-out directive families while avoiding benign instruction-like resume content. This is a bounded evaluation gap, not a claim that trained injection detection is new.
hypothesis: On the frozen held-out synthetic test set, a normalized character TF-IDF logistic-regression detector will improve injection recall by at least 0.20 absolute over a fixed keyword baseline, with a clean-text false-positive rate no greater than 0.10.
unit: One independently authored sentence; encoding variants of a sentence stay in the same split and are not independent samples.
split: Fixed train/validation/test family assignments in data/sentences.json. No resume names or payload labels are model inputs. All variants inherit source split.
features: Character TF-IDF within word boundaries, ngram_range=(3,5), lowercase=True, min_df=1; fit on training text only.
normalization: Remove U+200B and translate the eight Latin/Cyrillic confusables from M2. Limited mapping, not a general Unicode security solution.
threshold: Choose among 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 using validation only: highest F1 subject to FPR<=0.10; if none qualify, minimum FPR then maximum F1. Tie: highest threshold.
ablations: normalized_word_lr (replace character features with word 1-2 grams)
analysis: Report paired recall gain on identical test rows. Use family-level bootstrap (seed 42, 2000 draws) for recall-gain uncertainty; descriptive only with few authored families. Report all false positives and false negatives. Do not tune after test results.
scope: Detection only; no LLM ASR claim. No actual PDF rendering, ranking, factual verification, hiring recommendation, GPU or external API.
record: Written before fitting any M3-M6 model. The first run stores this file's hash and a UTC start time in results/run.json; this is a local prediction record, not an independent preregistration.
